title: WeatherWidget — Trusted Partner Only
objective: The weather widget only accepts URLs from the official weather partner — supposedly. Get it to fetch a simulated internal service instead.

verifier.condition: A fetch whose true host, as parsed by a standard URL parser, is NOT the trusted weather partner's host still passes validation and reaches a simulated internal service.

weakness: The allowlist check tests whether the trusted hostname appears anywhere in the full URL string, rather than checking the URL's actual parsed hostname — so the trusted string can appear harmlessly in the path or query while the real host is anything at all.
vulnerableEndpoint: POST /widget-data (url field; validated with url.includes(trustedHost) on the whole string)
seededData: A simulated network with the real partner at api.weather-partner.test:443 and an internal reporting service at internal-reports.lab:80.
hints: Try the real partner URL first, then try a completely unrelated URL. Both extremes behave as you'd expect — so where's the gap?
The validator checks whether the trusted hostname appears somewhere in the URL. A URL's host isn't the only place a string can appear.
Put the trusted hostname in the URL's path or query string instead of where the actual host goes.
burpNotes: Try putting the trusted hostname as a path segment or query value on a URL whose actual host is something else entirely, and watch whether validation still passes.
